Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

nonsense! interjection

also rubbish, hogwash, that’s hogwash!, rubbish!, trash (nonsense), baloney!, stuff and nonsense, cut out the nonsense, that’s a lot of nonsense, you are talking nonsense, stop talking nonsense, rubbish!, fiddlesticks!, no nonsense!, stuff (junk)

classical

Traupman 104
Plaut. Truc. 861: Aufer nūgās
Plaut. Men. 621: Nūgās agis
Traupman 114

Nūgās!

Other words

  • Nūgae!

    also used · classical · Traupman 104; Traupman 314

  • Quisquiliae! — rubbish!

    also used · modern · Traupman 107: rubbish!, quisquiliae!

    The word is “sweepings, rubbish” (see rubbish); as an exclamation it is Traupman’s. Nūgās! is the comic word. Lewis & Short gives quisquiliae as sweepings, refuse, rubbish, and figuratively of worthless people; as an exclamation it is Traupman’s. The comic poets say nūgās!.

  • Fābulae! — stuff! nonsense! baloney!

    also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 2.3.95; And. 1.3.19 (Lewis & Short s.v. fābula); Traupman 93

    Literally “stories!”

  • nūgās garrīre — talk nonsense

    also used · classical · Plaut. Curc. 5.2.6: Nūgās garrīs. — Soleō. (Lewis & Short s.v. soleō); Traupman 104: you are talking nonsense, nūgās garrīs

  • Omitte nūgās! — cut out the nonsense!

    also used · modern · Traupman 104: cut out the nonsense, omitte nūgās; Traupman 33

    Traupman’s phrase, built like Plautus’ aufer nūgās (above), which says the same thing in attested words.

  • Gerrae! — rubbish! stuff and nonsense!

    also used · classical · Plaut. Asin. 600: gerrae!; Plaut. Poen. 137: gerrae germānae

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

    Greek γέρρα, wickerwork; Festus tells how it came to mean trifles (Lewis & Short).

  • Hariolāre. — you’re raving; you’re talking through your hat (literally, you’re prophesying)

    also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 492: Hariolāre.

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Examples

  • Nūgās garrīs. — Soleō.

    You’re talking nonsense. — I usually do.Plaut. Curc. 5.2.6 (Lewis & Short s.v. soleō)

  • Nūgae sunt istae magnae.

    That’s a lot of nonsense.Traupman 104

  • Nē nūgāre!

    No nonsense!Traupman 351

  • Quisquiliae!

    Rubbish!Traupman 372

  • lēgēs ut cōnscrībat, quibus sē populus teneat. Gerrae!

    to draft laws for the people to keep. Rubbish!Plaut. Asin. 600

See also don’t be silly!.
